text: 00:00 Adhan (aya al-sala and aya al-fala included) 01:00 Another person giving sermon  02:00 Appears to be the person talking about Adam and Eve in Paradise making the human forget  Allah is the greatest.  Allah is the greatest.  There is no god but Allah.  This is still the continuation of the last khutba, the finish of khutba al-tahraf.  Although they never ended, this is what they had last time.  They found out or analyzed that Adam's distribution was not meaningful.  It was not a malicious form of distribution.  We can even go further and say that Adam had no intention of transgression.  Actually, it is clear in the Qur'an, in surah 20, verse 116, that what happened to Adam was that he forgot.  He was not strong enough. He forgot.  We also learn in surah 6, verse 68, in surah 12, verse 42, in surah 18, verse 63, in surah 58, verse 19 and so on,  that the creature that makes us forget the most important thing is no less than shaitan himself.  Shaitan makes us forget.  And thus we can conclude from the basis of these verses that I have enumerated,  it was shaitan who made poor Adam, our great great grandfather, forget.  I think there is not much speculation to that point.  However, the fact that Adam forgot, even temporarily,  this has to assume that he has forgotten something that he knew.  You cannot forget something that you never knew or you never know.  And thus we have some speculation last time, and I submitted to you brothers and sisters,  that what Adam forgot was what Allah SWT taught him.  And as you know, in surah 2, verse 31, it is very clear.  Allah taught Adam all the names.  I admit there was some tafsir or commentary on this point.  I went further and said that these names which Allah taught Adam,  have to do with Allah himself.  Who Allah is, what Allah is,  His power, more important, that He is the source of all power.  And knowing these qualities of Allah, denoted by His names,  gives us a profound, a deep form of knowledge.  It makes us understand the signs, the ayahs around us.  And not only the signs around us, but the signs within us.  Quran speaks of the signs outside us, without and within.  And if we know Allah's manifestations without and within us,  the high form of knowledge that I am insisting,  we will be able to see all phenomena in the blue light.  Natural phenomena, both physical and biological, and within ourselves.  Psychological phenomena, and what this psychological phenomena brings about.  Individual and social phenomena.  And as I mentioned last time, all of these things,  our birth, our childhood, our youth, our death,  our love, our petty hatred, our resentment, emotions, regulations,  all of these things, even warfare between groups and so on,  all of these represent manifestations of Allah's creative power.  He is the ruler, He rules everything, and nothing can happen without His will.  Then we talk also of Allah breathing something of His Spirit into Adam.  It is very interesting.  On at least three points, Quran says that Allah breathed into Adam something,  mean, the Arabic word is mean, blew him from His Spirit.  So this is very important.  He didn't say He blew His Spirit, because then Allah will be creating other Allahs,  which is a contradiction.  Something.  What does this mean?  Well, we have this in surah 15, verse 39, in surah 32, verse 9, and in surah 38, verse 72.  And this is what I believe, it is up to you to reflect on what I am saying,  to accept or reject my views, or to use my views as a point of departure,  for you to go deeper into it, or find an alternative interpretation.  My interpretation is that the breathing into Adam something of His Spirit,  Allah's Spirit, would be the foundation.  First.  The capacity.  The capacity to know.  To know the names themselves.  For if man does not have the capacity to know the names, he cannot know.  This is very clear.  Let's say, A, he was raised.  In other words, Allah has given him the capacity for knowledge,  and special knowledge, knowledge to know about Allah Himself.  Allah is so great, nothing can know Allah,  unless that something who knows Allah, has something given to him by Allah.  I hope this is very clear.  It is a philosophical proof.  You cannot know Allah, unless Allah Himself has given you the power to know Him.  Because He is so great, and so above us.  No one less than Allah can know Him.  But Allah gave man His part of His breath.  And this breath of Allah in us, is what allows us to know Allah.  Now this is a very profound view.  I hope you will not forget it.  But more than that,  it is not just a matter of giving man the power to know Him,  Allah, I believe, has given us certain capacities to manifest  some of the qualities which we attribute to Him.  And the Quran is full of these attributes.  When the Quran says that Allah destroys,  we don't know we can destroy, can we destroy?  Why will we destroy things day after day?  And so, we have now capacities.  This, I think, is a second but just as important meaning of the breath of Allah in us.  And it is not that we just have these capacities.  Because a capacity can remain a capacity.  There must be certain actualities in the relation between Allah and mankind  such that these qualities can become what we would call actual.  In other words, we may have the capacity to feel pity or to love,  but that capacity can always, will always remain a capacity.  Unless there is something that will actualize that capacity into something that is real.  So, if we have the capacity for mercy, that capacity will remain a capacity.  It can only be actualized on account of certain forces.  Allah Himself can help us or His Messengers can teach us how to actualize this capacity.  Incidentally, this point shows the necessity of revelation.  So, I think we have said so much about these powers to know,  these powers to be created, these powers to destroy,  these powers to have pity and to sympathize,  the ability to have what we call this fine sense of consideration.  And again, we say that this breath from Allah in mankind  represents the most important part of man's complex nature.  Man is composed of clay, but he also has life in him.  We have given that to the soul.  But we also say, based on the Qur'an,  that he partakes of the breath or the spirit of Allah.  This spirit in mankind is the highest part,  the most excellent part of man's soul for now.  It cannot be otherwise, for it comes from Allah Himself.  It does not belong to us, although we are utilizing it.  And now we can understand deeper some of these verses in the Qur'an.  When Adam and Eve said to Allah,  Allah, we have wronged ourselves.  We have wronged ourselves.  What did they wrong?  Their feet, stomach, hair and so on?  It could be that.  They realized that they had wronged the most important part of themselves,  that part which belonged to Allah.  And in trying to harm that part of Allah,  but utterly they ended up hurting themselves,  because no one can harm Allah.  So if you are angry, if you insult Allah,  you are not harming Allah, you are harming yourself.  So, when you harm or be gay,  this spirit that Allah has blessed into us,  in the long run, we are harming ourselves.  The breath of Allah in Adam and Eve,  as well as the knowledge taught by Allah to them,  were not given their proper due.  But it was the recognition of this,  of this mistake,  that made Adam repent.  And as we all know,  since Allah is the All-Merciful,  and in response to this repentance,  Allah presented towards Adam,  gave words of revelation to him,  and more important for us now,  He promised mankind revelation,  or descending of a guidance.  In brief,  what Allah promised Adam,  and His descendants, mankind,  all of us,  are reminders.  And what are these reminders?  By definition, a reminder is something  to counteract and protect from them.  Because man was created weak,  that is, he was not created as a god,  and therefore he forgets.  But Allah puts necessary mechanisms.  They are as follows.  Descending of Prophets,  these are forms of reminders.  They are what you call,  Remembrances.  And the Prophet Muhammad is called  a Remembrance.  Revelations are believable reminders.  The Quran is the perfect reminder.  And Salat is a technique  not to forget,  which means the same,  as saying that Salat, prayer,  is a technique to keep on reminding us.  And you will find it in Surah 20,  verse 14,  and Surah 76,  verses 25 and 26.  Thus,  Shaitan, as the source of forgetfulness,  forgetfulness is an enemy  of Prophets.  Shaitan is an enemy of Revelation.  Shaitan is an enemy of the Quran.  And Shaitan is  the greatest enemy of Salat.  One of his main jobs  on earth is precisely  to make man forget  all of these things  that we have just mentioned.  But now,  we are getting tired of talking about Shaitan.  Let's go back to  the breath of Allah.  Let's relate the breath of Allah  and his teaching of beliefs to Adam  to the purpose of man's creation.  Quran says,  in Surah 6,  verse 102,  in Surah 20, verse 14,  in Surah 51,  verse 56 and so on,  very clear  that  Allah created man  to worship  or serve him.  The word here,  in Arabic word,  the verb is  to serve.  This reveals  immediately to us  that creation is  and one of the meanings of  when Allah is called  is that  He creates with  a purpose.  And since Allah creates with a purpose,  certainly,  He must in some way or another  reveal to man  the nature of this purpose.  Either by putting in man's nature  a kind of primeval knowledge  or by revelation.  For example,  if you get,  you want to build a house,  when you get a carpenter,  when you bring him to the land,  when you have to tell him  what to do,  what is it going to be,  a brick house,  a wooden house,  or a house made of adobe or so on.  You have to tell.  If you are rational  and if you are in a purposive manner,  you have to tell someone,  that carpenter,  what he is supposed to do.  You just don't give him,  put him in the land.  Same thing with Allah.  We have to show,  since He asks with a purpose,  that He already put His mechanism  in our nature.  If that is the case,  which is the case,  it is part of man's nature  already to recognize Allah.  But more than that,  Allah gives us revelation.  If He doesn't give us the knowledge,  at least the propensity  to accept such knowledge  when prophets appear.  And thus,  again,  I submit to you all,  that  in giving man  part of his breath  and in instilling in him  the capacity  or potentialities  to actualize  certain qualities,  now this is very important,  Allah makes it  a duty for man  to understand the names  and to make such potentialities  operative  or functional  in individual  and social life.  Now,  this is a very strong  statement.  That is,  I repeat,  if God has given you  the capacity  to be compassionate,  and if God has given us  the capacity  to be compassionate,  and more,  and follow,  it is a duty for us  to be compassionate  and to be patient.  Now, this is a very strong stand.  I don't know what  ethical philosophers  say about it.  But it is part of man's nature  because he has the breath of Allah  and Allah is compassionate.  When He breathed it onto us,  He gave us the capacity  to be compassionate.  Therefore, it is a duty for us  to develop our capacity  for compassion  and certainly for knowledge.  Allah is the knower.  And if Allah has given us  the power to know,  it becomes our duty  to know.  Therefore,  again,  it is part of worship  or part of service to Allah  to know what Allah is,  who He is,  what He is,  what He represents,  and to know more  why He created us.  But more than that,  as I mentioned earlier,  it is part of  ibadah,  of worship,  to develop  those capacities  which Allah  has given us.  But,  as we discussed  in the last goodbyes,  India  and mankind  for that matter,  use such capacities  in a manner showing  lack of restraint.  We forget.  In brief,  powers,  capacities  can be  misused  or abused.  Therefore,  I give an example.  The capacity for patience  sometimes can be used  as a trick  for revenge,  but that is not  what Allah wants us to do.  Compassion also  can be used  as a technique  to deceive people.  Therefore, it is not real  compassion.  Therefore,  it now becomes clear  to all of us  why instructions  must come  from Allah Himself  regarding  the use  of such powers,  the ends of such powers.  This is  one of the fundamental  meanings of revelation.  And if man has  no free will,  there will be no problem.  If man has no free will,  he will be just acting  A following B  following C  following D.  But no!  Man has alternative  by the nature  of his free will.  And it is this will  that can stifle  his potentialities  or actualize  his potentialities  towards selfish  or wrong ends.  Therefore,  it is  important for us  to have revelation.  And he  or she  who looks to Allah  as the source  of revelation  will have Allah  responding  to such persons.  And Allah  will give the correct  guidance.  The position  of Allah's breath  in man  is a test.  It is a test  as I have been  repeating  and over-repeating  on how  we should  develop  our potentialities  and have them  directed properly.  And Allah  has given us  the document  how to  actualize  his potentialities  and lead it  towards the destiny  that He has  prepared for us.  The more we develop  our potentialities  for the good,  that is,  the more we develop  our potentialities  in accordance  with Allah's guidance,  the more  our spirit grows.  Which is the same  as saying  the more  of Allah's breath  in us  is working.  All right?  I think this is  our whole  pathology.  It is like saying  A is equal to A  or 1 plus 1  is equal to 2.  The more  we develop  our potentialities  which Allah  gave us  for the good,  that is,  the more we are  listening or remembering  Allah,  the more  is our spirit  growing.  And since the spirit  is the highest form  of our soul,  the more  is our soul  growing.  Now,  Mustafa has been  always emphasizing  about the growth  of our soul.  I'm sure  he has his own  profound meaning  for what's meant  by our soul growth.  I'm only giving  one meaning,  one possible meaning  of what it means  to say  that the soul grows.  To me,  the soul grows  means  that the highest  portion  that comes from  Allah the spirit  is growing  or actualized.  So to put it  politically,  the more  of Allah's spirit  you have in you,  the more  divine elements  you have  in you.  The more  we remember  Allah  and do  what this  remembrance  entails in action,  the more  does the soul  grow.  Right?  Because the more  of Allah's spirit  is in us.  Therefore,  the more spiritual  we become.  So to say  in Islam,  so and so is spiritual  has a particular  meaning.  Let us not confuse it  with what other people  you know,  say about  so and so  spiritual.  We see that  with these  transcendental  people who follow  transcendentalism  and say,  oh,  this is very  spiritual.  Well,  I'm not the one  who is going  to fight with  these people  about the use  of the word  spiritual.  They have their  own meaning,  what spiritual  means.  The Jews and  the Christians,  I assume,  have also the  meaning of  spirituality.  But,  in terms of the  Quran,  we have a meaning  for what is  spiritual.  To us,  spiritual will  mean what?  The more  of Allah's spirit  in us.  And what does  this mean?  Very clear.  The more  we remember  Allah,  understand his  names,  understand the  manifestation of  his names in  nature,  without and  without us.  And therefore,  we can conclude  easily,  the less we  remember Allah,  the more our  soul will sink.  That is the  length of his  spirit will be  enough, right?  And,  also in another  way,  the less we  remember Allah,  the more his  breath  in us  will be  tightened.  We are not  allowing him  to act  alive.  And thus,  we can now  give a deeper  meaning to the  word righteousness  or taqwa.  It is this,  taqwa can mean,  righteousness,  can mean to us  now,  a consistent  and persevering  consciousness  of Allah,  Subhanallah to  Allah.  In Surah  91,  verse 7 to  7,  there is a  description of  the growth of  the soul.  And it says  that the  growing soul  is a soul  that knows  the difference  between  right and  wrong.  The assumption  is that the  person is  following the  right.  In Surah  62,  verse 2,  the Quran  speaks of  the functions  of messengers.  Messengers come  to help men  grow,  not grow  physically,  to grow  spiritually.  In Surah  2,  verse 139,  Ibrahim  prays to  Allah,  he prays  to Allah  to send  messengers  to teach  Muslims  in  scripture  and in  wisdom,  and to  teach man  what man  does not  know.  In Surah  2,  verse 151,  it's clearly  shown that  growth,  growth,  means growth  of the soul,  it means  knowledge  of the  scripture,  number one.  It means  gaining wisdom  or acquiring  wisdom from  such a  knowledge of  the scripture,  and important,  coming to  know  what man  did not  know before,  or what man  cannot know  through his  own efforts.  It is  knowledge that  can come only  to the help  of Allah.  And if we  go to  Surah  62,  verses  2 to 4,  in Surah  4,  verse 113,  here we  know deeper  the meaning  of Allah's  infinite  or boundless  grace,  for it  consists precisely  in giving  mankind  these three  things.  And you all  know what  it is,  it refers to  the greatest  name,  Dhu'l-Fadl-Azim.  Allah's  called  Dhu'l-Fadl-Azim  because  His  infinite  grace  consists  precisely  in  teaching us  the  scripture,  allowing us  to have  wisdom  from  following  this  scripture.  In other  words,  we can  say one  of the  greatest  gifts of  Allah is  precisely  giving us  the techniques  to counteract  forgetfulness  so that we  do not fall  into the  trap of  poor  ancestor  A.  Now it  also becomes  easy for  us to  understand  what the  Quran means  when it  says that  those who  forget Allah  forget their  souls.  That is  Surah 59,  19.  You see how  beautiful the  Quran is,  very consistent.  Those who  forget Allah  forget their  souls.  As I  told you  earlier,  you cannot  know Allah  unless Allah  gives you the  power to know  Him.  Allah is so  great,  no one,  nothing can  know Allah  unless Allah  Himself put  something in  Him on that  thing to know  Him.  This is the  meaning of  knowledge.  The contact  between the  knower and  the known  is the  relation of  knowing.  Allah has  given us  the power  to know  Him.  But those  who  insist in  rejecting Allah,  who in effect,  even if they  say Allah,  Allah, Allah  20,000 times  a day,  if they don't  mean it,  they forget  their souls.  Why?  Because the  soul, as we  mentioned so  many times,  is the most  important part  of man.  It is the  part in man  which represents  part of Allah,  spirit in him.  Therefore to  say that  Mr. X  forgets Allah  is the same as  saying that  Mr. X forgets  his soul.  This is again  another topology.  It's like saying  A is A  or 1 plus  1 is 2.  In Surah  20,  124,  saying that  he who forgets  Allah will be  blind in the  last day.  In the same  Surah 20,  verse 136,  saying that  those who  forget Allah's  revelation will  be forgotten  by Allah in  the last day.  Same thing in  Surah 45,  verse 34.  All this  means that  such individuals  will be lost  in the last  day.  It also  means that  their souls  have shrunk  and for all  practical purposes  disappeared.  They are  just pure  clay.  It also  means that  the most  essential part  is some  other forms  of clay.  And poor  Adam,  he forgot  Allah.  But Alhamdulillah,  he was able  to remember  again.  He was fast.  I suppose so.  Good for him  and for his  descendants.  For when he  found out he  was abandoned  by Shaitan,  he immediately  turned to Allah.  And Allah  gives  mankind  the instruments  to counteract  forgetfulness.  This is up to  us.  But I don't  know really  how fast  Adam  repented.  Maybe I've been  influenced by  those times  when he says,  repent fast!  Did you say  that last time?  Did you say  repent fast?  By the way,  with your permission,  I would like to  tell you a story.  You know the  Arabs,  they are  very interesting  and wonderful  people.  They have  many poems  and stories.  They combine  Quran with  common law  with the  Qur'an  for Adam.  They tell  a story  which I  don't remember  very well.  They say  there are  about six  things  or seven  things  that a man  can do  in a hurry.  I'll put it  another way.  The Arabs  say,  take it easy  in everything.  Don't  hurry!  Except in  around six  or seven  things.  I don't  remember  the six  or seven  things.  But I read it  many years ago.  But this is what  I remember.  The Arabs  say,  go slow,  except  when you  commit a sin,  immediately ask  repentance from Allah.  As you can see,  this is Qur'an.  Number two,  when your guests  come to your  house and  they're hungry,  immediately feed  them.  Don't  take it easy.  This is Arab  hospitality.  The third  one is,  if you ask  for a person's  money,  please pay  your debts.  This is common  sense.  Before the  sun  goes down,  when a man  dies,  hurry up with  his burial  before he  stinks. But anyhow,  to go back to  the  football,  here you  can see that  the  haqiqa really  summarizes very  well everything  that we have  said,  that Allah  is the  Lord of the  worlds,  the creator  therefore of  mankind,  but the  master of  the day of  judgment.  We need  his help  and guidance  and we pray  to him for  it.  In other words,  we assume,  we accept from  him that we  need his help  and therefore we  want his  revelation.
